mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by 2% or more.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 1% or more for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO declines by 1%+ for four straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% from the previous month signals a broad-based demand collapse, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by >0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of episodes where both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by >0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a flat or falling unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tight labor market that boosts wage inflation and input costs, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in a non-recessionary regime.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average and UNRATE ≤ previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of tight labor market as defined above in non-recessionary regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 0.5% or more for five consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which raises earnings expectations and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises by ≥0.5% for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when INDPRO rises by ≥0.5% for five straight months.
